newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end down on technicals, deliveries.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end down on technicals, deliveries.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on the posting Thursday of 3.4 million bushels of soybeans for delivery on the November contract, traders said.
The market also was hit by broad-based fund selling, tied to a technical collapse, and nearby November touched a session low of $6.66 per bushel, an 11-month low.

"The technical picture continues to dominate in spite of another week of respective sales (exports)," said Mark Cermak of Chicago trade house O'Connor and Co. Also "the market is more concerned about the potential for a bigger crop than it is with demand right now."
Sell stops were hit when November broke support at $6.71-1/2 and January fell below support at $6.79. "That brought in another wave of fund selling," Cermak said.
"There is good harvest weather for corn and beans and there were big deliveries," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Traders were expecting from two to three million bushels of soybeans to be posted but also were expecting strong stopping of the deliveries.
Soybeans closed 15-1/2 to 24 cents per bushel lower, with November down 21-3/4 at $6.67-3/4.
There was weak and scattered stopping of the deliveries which exacerbated the slide.
"The deliveries tell us there may be more beans available than we thought," a trader said. "Export sales were okay but seasonally they should be."
USDA Thursday said the U.S. soybean net exports for the week ended October 24 totaled 810,100 tonnes, above trade expectations for 400,000 to 600,000 tonnes.
Technical traders said the soybean market remains in a downtrend with key moving averages giving off bearish signals.
Key players included late sales of five million bushels in the January by FIMAT Futures, traders said. Prudential Securities and Refco Inc each sold four million bushels of January, sources said.

Action in the soybean options pit also was noted with Refco Inc taking a bearish stance by purchasing 500 January $6.50 puts at 5-1/2 cents, 400 January $6.75 puts at 11-3/4 to 13 cents and bought 200 January $7.25 puts at 46 cents, traders said.
Continental Grain bought 200 March $6.50 puts and sold 200 March $7.75 puts at 3-1/2 cents and sold 200 March $7.00 calls at 21-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 95,000 contracts, up from 85,324 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, up from 11,440 Wednesday.
